questions.q: The IP address 127.0.0.1 is used for:
options: Loopback testing of the local machine
questions.solution: 127.x.x.x (typically 127.0.0.1 = localhost) loops packets back to the sender's own TCP/IP stack for self-testing.

questions.q: Which key runs the spelling and grammar check in MS Word?
questions.solution: **F7 = Spelling & Grammar**. F5 starts a slideshow in PowerPoint but in Word it opens Go To.

questions.q:
Match the medium to its technology:
A. HDD  B. Blu-ray  C. Pen drive  D. LTO tape
options: A-magnetic platters, B-optical laser, C-flash chips, D-magnetic tape
A-flash chips, B-magnetic platters, C-optical laser, D-magnetic tape
A-magnetic tape, B-flash chips, C-optical laser, D-magnetic platters
A-magnetic platters, B-optical laser, C-magnetic tape, D-flash chips
questions.solution: HDD spins magnetised platters; Blu-ray is read by a blue-violet laser; the pen drive is flash chips; LTO is archival magnetic tape — one example of each family.

questions.q: Which topology connects every node to a central hub or switch?
questions.solution: **Star topology** — all nodes hang off one central device.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said to me, "Please lend me your pen."
options: He requested me to lend him my pen.
He requested me to lend me your pen.
He ordered me to lend him my pen.
He said to me please to lend him my pen.
questions.solution: Please → **requested**; to lend + him (speaker) + my (listener). B leaves both pronouns direct; C mismatches tone (ordered for a request); D has no sentence structure.
questions.shortcut: please sets the verb: requested; then him + my.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: No sooner had the train left
questions.solution: The frozen pair is **no sooner…than**: 'No sooner had the train left **than** the passengers began…'. 'When' belongs with hardly/scarcely.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Keep the **e** before -able: noticeable. The e protects the soft 'c' sound (notice → notice-able). Noticable is the planted drop.
questions.shortcut: Keep-e rule: soft c needs its e.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The chairman, along with the directors, **were** inspecting the plant when the auditors arrived.
questions.solution: 'Along with' only adds information; the subject stays **the chairman** → **was inspecting**. The narration is past, so the present helpers in options 3 and 4 are out at once.

questions.q: The **Ryder Cup** is a team competition in which sport, contested between the USA and Europe?
questions.solution: The **Ryder Cup** is golf's USA v Europe biennial match; the Davis Cup is tennis's equivalent for nations.

questions.q: The **Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna)** of Rigvedic tradition was fought on the river —
questions.solution: The Dasarajna (Mandala VII) was fought on the **Parushni = Ravi**. **Sudas** of the Bharata clan defeated a confederacy of ten kings.

questions.q:
Match:
1. Rakhi bandhan as protest — Rabindranath Tagore
2. *Amar Sonar Bangla* — composed during Swadeshi agitation
3. National Council of Education — 1906
Which are correct?
questions.solution: All three are Swadeshi-era facts: Tagore's Rakhi tying and later the song (now Bangladesh's anthem), and the **National Council of Education (1906)** for national education.

questions.q: Which of the following substances undergoes sublimation?
questions.solution: **Camphor** changes directly from solid to vapour — **sublimation**. Naphthalene, iodine, ammonium chloride and dry ice also sublime.

questions.q: Rice at ₹30 per kg and ₹40 per kg are mixed in the ratio 2:3, and the mixture is sold at ₹45 per kg. The profit per cent is:
questions.shortcut: 20% would use SP ₹43.20 — the blend CP is ₹36.

questions.q: For $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$, the inequality $\sin\theta > \cos\theta$ holds when:
questions.solution: $\sin$ rises and $\cos$ falls; they cross at $45^\circ$. Beyond it, $\sin$ is on top.
questions.shortcut: $\theta > 45^\circ$. Trap: $<$ — the directions of the two functions are easy to swap.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have sides $8$ cm, $6$ cm, $4$ cm and $10$ cm, $7.5$ cm, $x$ cm (in corresponding order). The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
Corresponding pairs: $\frac{10}{8} = \frac{7.5}{6} = \frac{x}{4} = 1.25$.

$x = 4 \times 1.25 = 5$ cm.
questions.shortcut: One scale for all sides: $k = 1.25$ → $x = 5$ cm. Check the middle pair: $6 \times 1.25 = 7.5$ ✓.

questions.q: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.solution:
Faces 5 and 6 qualify: two of six.
$P = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Chalk, Charm, Chart, Chase, Chatter.** Which is the **fourth** word?
questions.solution: All share CHA. 4th letters: l (Chalk), r (Charm, Chart), s (Chase), t (Chatter); l < r < s < t. The r-pair: 5th letters m (Charm) vs t (Chart) → Charm first. Full order: Chalk, Charm, Chart, Chase, Chatter → fourth = **Chase**.
questions.shortcut: Sort the 4th letters; only the r-pair needs one more letter.

questions.q:
Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out. (The letters follow English alphabetical order.)

**OPQR, UVWX, ABCD, STUV**
questions.solution: All four are four consecutive letters and each contains exactly one vowel. In OPQR, UVWX and ABCD the vowel is the **first** letter. In STUV the vowel U is third → **STUV**.

questions.q: Which diagram correctly represents **Multiples of 5, Multiples of 7 and Multiples of 35**?
options: Two intersecting circles inside a third circle
Three nested circles, one inside the next
Two separate circles, with the third intersecting both
Two intersecting circles, with the third inside their common part
questions.solution: 35 = 5 × 7, so every multiple of 35 is a multiple of both 5 and 7. Multiples of 5 and 7 overlap (35, 70) but neither contains the other (10, 14). Answer: **two intersecting circles, with the third inside their common part**.
questions.shortcut: A common multiple sits in the overlap.

questions.q: Which word comes **first** in the dictionary?
questions.solution: All share MAR. 4th letters: b (Marble), k (Market), g (Margin). b is earliest → **Marble** comes first.
questions.shortcut: Ignore the shared part; only the first differing letter votes.
